result.summary: The street environment is characterized by a lack of formal pedestrian infrastructure, featuring unmarked roadways and discontinuous or poorly maintained sidewalks. The presence of vacant lots and a lack of traffic calming measures or marked crossings creates a high-risk environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Discontinuous Sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left side of the image transitions into an unpaved dirt path, forcing pedestrians into the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of Roadway Markings
hazards.description: The absence of center lines or lane markings can lead to unpredictable vehicle positioning and higher speeds.

hazards.name: Utility Pole Obstruction
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly within the narrow walking path on the left side.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side along the sidewalk line

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion and Widening
interventions.description: Pave the missing sidewalk sections and widen existing walkways to a minimum of 5-6 feet to ensure ADA compliance and safety.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks at intersections and use curb extensions to reduce crossing distances and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Roadway Striping
interventions.description: Add center lines and parking lane markings to organize traffic flow and naturally narrow the perceived travel lane to slow vehicles.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a wide but severely degraded sidewalk adjacent to a vacant lot and a blank building wall. The walkway is marred by significant cracking, uneven surfaces, and accumulated debris, with no physical buffer separating pedestrians from the roadway.

hazards.name: Degraded Sidewalk Surface
hazards.description: Extensive cracking and uneven pavement sections create significant tripping hazards for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Accumulated Debris
hazards.description: Trash and organic litter are scattered across the sidewalk, obstructing the clear path.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the fence line and sidewalk edge

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no furnishing zone or physical barrier between the walking path and the active travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Edge of the sidewalk adjacent to the road

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Full resurfacing of the walkway to provide a smooth, level, and ADA-compliant pedestrian path.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furnishing Zone
interventions.description: Implement a planting strip with street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install lighting to improve visibility and safety along the blank frontage of the vacant lot.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by narrow, degraded sidewalks and a lack of clear separation from the roadway. While stop signs are present at the intersection, faded crosswalk markings and the presence of large vacant lots create a sparse, auto-oriented atmosphere.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk at the intersection is significantly worn, reducing its visibility to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Degraded sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left side appears to be unpaved or severely degraded, creating a tripping hazard and accessibility barrier.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian buffer
hazards.description: Pedestrians walk directly adjacent to the travel lane without any physical buffer like a planting strip or parked cars in the immediate foreground.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Apply continental or ladder-style thermoplastic markings to the intersection to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Sidewalk reconstruction
interventions.description: Repair and widen the existing walkways to provide a continuous, ADA-compliant path on both sides of the street.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide but severely degraded sidewalk with significant cracking and uneven surfaces. There is no physical buffer between the walkway and the roadway, and no street lighting or traffic calming measures are visible in this mid-block section.

hazards.name: Degraded Sidewalk Surface
hazards.description: The sidewalk is heavily cracked and uneven, creating significant trip hazards for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Walkway Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash bins and utility items are placed directly on the walking path, narrowing the effective width.

hazards.name: Lack of Street Lighting
hazards.description: No street lights are visible, which may compromise pedestrian safety and security after dark.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Repave the sidewalk to provide a smooth, ADA-compliant walking surface free of trip hazards.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians at night.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Formalize a planting strip or buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway to protect pedestrians from moving traffic.
